newsitem.title: USA: Bayer unit to expand plasma capacity.
newsitem.headline: Bayer unit to expand plasma capacity.

text.p: Bayer Corp, a unit of Bayer AG, said Sunday it will invest $60 million to expand its plasma fractionation capacity at its Clayton, N.C. plant.
In a statement, the company said that the investment to be made over the next six years will increase capacity by 15 percent.

In a three-part plan to raise capacity, Bayer said it has initially set up a new immune globulin intravenous (IGIV) process that will allow the fractionation of an additional 300,000 liters of plasma per year.
An additional process improvement under development which will allow Bayer to significantly increase IGIV yield by as much as 40 percent, it said.
It will also use its new plant in Rosia, Italy, to fractionate plasma, adding 500,000 liters of capacity to meet rising worldwide demand, it said.
